notes.summary: MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) gives 4–6 questions in Tier 2. Most are keyboard shortcuts (standard Windows ones), Excel functions and cell references, file extensions, and PowerPoint slide-show keys.

concepts.title: Common shortcuts (Windows)
concepts.body:
KeysAction
Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+VCopy / Cut / Paste
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+YUndo / Redo
Ctrl+B / Ctrl+I / Ctrl+UBold / Italic / Underline
Ctrl+S / Ctrl+O / Ctrl+N / Ctrl+PSave / Open / New / Print
Ctrl+F / Ctrl+HFind / Replace
Ctrl+ASelect all
Ctrl+KInsert hyperlink
F12Save As

concepts.title: MS Word
concepts.body:
• Alignment: Ctrl+L left, Ctrl+E centre, Ctrl+R right, Ctrl+J justify.
  • Ctrl+Enter page break; F7 spelling and grammar; Shift+F3 change case; Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[ increase / decrease font size by 1 point.
  • Default extension: .docx (older .doc); templates .dotx.

concepts.title: MS Excel
concepts.body:
• A cell address is column letter + row number (e.g. B3). A range is written A1:A10.
  • References: A1 relative, $A$1 absolute, $A1 / A$1 mixed. F4 cycles through them.
  • F2 edit cell; Ctrl+; current date; Ctrl+Shift+; current time; Alt+= AutoSum; Shift+F11 new worksheet.
  • COUNT counts numbers only; COUNTA counts all non-empty cells; COUNTBLANK counts empty cells.
  • Every formula starts with =. Extension .xlsx.

concepts.title: MS PowerPoint
concepts.body:
• F5 starts the slide show from the first slide; Shift+F5 from the current slide; Esc ends it.
  • Ctrl+M inserts a new slide.
  • Views: Normal, Slide Sorter, Reading, Slide Show, Outline.
  • Extension .pptx; show file .ppsx.

varieties.name: MS Word shortcuts and features
varieties.how: Learn the alignment set (L, E, R, J) and the formatting set (B, I, U) as groups.

example.q: Which shortcut right-aligns a paragraph in MS Word?
steps: Alignment keys: L = left, E = centre, R = right, J = justify.

varieties.name: Excel functions, references and keys
varieties.how: Read the function name carefully (COUNT vs COUNTA) and check which cells are numbers, text or blank.

example.q: Cells A1:A4 contain 5, 10, 15 and 20. What does =AVERAGE(A1:A4) return?

varieties.name: PowerPoint keys and views
varieties.how: F5 = from beginning, Shift+F5 = from current slide, Ctrl+M = new slide.

example.q: Which key ends a running slide show?
steps: Esc leaves the slide show and returns to the previous view.

tips: Ctrl+E is centre in Word; in Excel 2013+ it is Flash Fill.
Ctrl+H opens Replace in Word and Excel.
In Excel, ##### in a cell means the column is too narrow for the number.
traps: Ctrl+; inserts the date; Ctrl+Shift+; inserts the time.
F5 in Word opens Go To, but F5 in PowerPoint starts the slide show.
COUNT ignores text; COUNTA counts text too.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut makes selected text bold in MS Word?
questions.solution: Ctrl+B = Bold, Ctrl+I = Italic, Ctrl+U = Underline.

questions.q: The shortcut Ctrl+Z is used to:
questions.solution: Ctrl+Z undoes the last action. Ctrl+Y redoes it.

questions.q: In MS PowerPoint, which key starts the slide show from the first slide?
questions.solution: F5 starts the slide show from the beginning. Shift+F5 starts from the current slide.

questions.q: In MS Excel, the reference $A$1 is a(n):
questions.solution: The $ sign before both the column (A) and the row (1) locks both, so $A$1 is an absolute reference. It does not change when the formula is copied.

questions.q: In MS Word, Ctrl+J is used to:
questions.solution: Ctrl+J aligns text to both left and right margins (justify). Ctrl+E is centre and Ctrl+K inserts a hyperlink.

questions.q: Which shortcut inserts the current date in an Excel cell?
questions.solution: Ctrl+; (semicolon) enters today's date. Ctrl+Shift+; enters the current time, Ctrl+D fills down and Alt+= is AutoSum.

questions.q: In Excel, A1 = 10, A2 = 20, A3 = "abc", A4 is blank and A5 = 30. What does =COUNTA(A1:A5) return?
questions.solution: COUNTA counts every non-empty cell: A1, A2, A3 (text) and A5 = 4 cells. (=COUNT would give 3 because it counts numbers only.)

questions.q: Which shortcut starts a PowerPoint slide show from the current slide?
questions.solution: Shift+F5 starts the show from the slide you are on. F5 alone starts from slide 1.
